# ISSUE-329 packaging plan

Ship the existing Linux helper alongside the CLI through local Make targets and release archives. This is packaging only; helper acceptance, discovery, bounded diagnostics, protocol, adapters, and all resource limits remain with #318. No runtime source or runtime tests change.

## Dimensions

Risk is approved as sensitive; no size or uncertainty is set. Advisory size: small; uncertainty: moderate (release archive grouping). One plan/implement/validate cycle should fit the 16-hour total claim budget. Use the configured independent agent plan review and require independent review of packaging regressions and release evidence.

## What we know

- `Makefile:8-23` supports GO, GOBIN and BIN_DIR overrides, builds/installs only the CLI, and intentionally avoids local version stamping (`Makefile:3-6`).
- `.goreleaser.yaml:5-37` builds the CLI with CGO disabled for Linux/Darwin/Windows amd64/arm64, stamps Version/Commit/Date, and uses tar.gz except Windows zip. There is one archive definition.
- `cmd/swarm-restore-helper/main.go:1-13` is an existing internal entry point; packaging must compile this package unchanged.
- `README.md:75-92` and `docs/project.md:9` advertise standalone Go installation; the latter also recommends `go build -o swarm ./cmd/swarm`. These install the CLI only. README documents release versus local metadata.
- `docs/developer.md:620-627` requires one `- ` bullet per fragment under `changes/unreleased/`; Makefile changelog-check runs `go run ./cmd/changelog --check`.
- `internal/sandbox/restore.go:29-33` requires an explicitly supplied helper; packaging must not imply automatic discovery or runtime use.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:56-60` pins GoReleaser v2.18.3 for snapshots; workflow changes are unnecessary.
- `internal/cli/version_test.go:8,68` covers version resolution. Existing helper tests in `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go:25,104` test runtime behavior and are outside this task.
- `go.mod` already provides yaml.v3. Go and make are available; GoReleaser is absent (`command -v`). This snapshot has no accessible Git repository (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails).

## What we're assuming

- GoReleaser v2.18.3 can group unequal per-platform build sets in the existing archive definition using `allow_different_binary_count` and explicit build IDs. Check this against that version's schema/help and the operator snapshot run; never assume a config parsing test proves archive generation.
- Native Linux packaging tests can build without network when dependencies are cached. Check with focused tests, report environment failures separately, and retain the operator archive checklist.

## Open questions

- Actual GoReleaser archive membership and modes require a GoReleaser-equipped operator or release environment; the TEST_PLAN checklist answers this without blocking implementation on unavailable services.
- New test-path absence at the approved base cannot be established via Git in this snapshot. `internal/packaging` and `changes/unreleased/329.md` are absent locally. Before creating either proposed new file, developer/coordinator checks the approved base tree; if present, modify it instead of calling it new. No production scope expansion is needed.

## Architectural context and exact touchpoints

The helper source exists, but neither installation channel includes it. Change only `Makefile` build/install targets and target comments, `.goreleaser.yaml` builds/archives, `README.md` and `docs/project.md:9` installation guidance, proposed `changes/unreleased/329.md` (one packaging-scoped bullet), and proposed `internal/packaging/packaging_test.go` (test-only package; absent in the supplied snapshot, subject to base check above). No new dependencies or release workflow changes.

## Implementation sequence

1. Extend Make build/install to compile/install `./cmd/swarm-restore-helper` only for the effective Go target OS Linux. Resolve target OS using the selected GO tool (`go env GOOS`), respecting caller overrides. Set `CGO_ENABLED=0` on the helper invocation even when caller environment enables cgo; do not change CLI flags, metadata or cgo selection. Keep both products from this checkout, honor BIN_DIR/GOBIN/GO, quote output/install paths, preserve the installed CLI version invocation and its existing cross-install limitations. Darwin/Windows retain CLI-only behavior. Do not add downloads or fallback behavior.
2. Add a Linux-only helper release build for amd64/arm64 with explicit CGO_ENABLED=0, correct binary name and existing helper main package. Keep CLI matrix and release ldflags unchanged. Explicitly select both build IDs with the supported v2 archive `ids:` key (not deprecated `builds:`) in archives and use the supported unequal-count option so Linux gets two matching binaries while Darwin/Windows get only their CLI. Preserve archive names, formats, documentation files and checksum behavior. Confirm option compatibility with v2.18.3 during operator validation.
3. Add test-only packaging regressions: parse the real YAML with typed fields asserting archive `ids` and rejecting deprecated archive `builds`, assert complete OS/arch/build/archive contracts, and exercise Make targets in temporary output directories. Inspect actual helper build info with debug/buildinfo (CGO_ENABLED=0, target OS/arch, main package) and executable mode; compare CLI module/build metadata with an unstamped same-checkout control. Use a recording GO wrapper for deterministic Make command/environment tests, including ambient CGO_ENABLED=1, effective non-Linux targets, custom paths with spaces and helper failure propagation. Wrapper tests must not substitute for real Linux artifact checks. Assert malformed config fixtures (omitted helper build/archive ID, missing cgo override, wrong OS/arch) are rejected. Add automated temporary-Makefile mutations removing the helper recipe or removing/changing its CGO_ENABLED=0 override, separately for build and install; run each with the recording wrapper under ambient CGO_ENABLED=1 and require the shared packaging assertion to reject it. Confirm the unmodified fixture passes, so a syntax error or unrelated command failure is not counted as mutation detection. Never run the helper restore protocol.
4. Update README and the `docs/project.md:9` installation paragraph together to recommend Linux release pairs or `make install` from one checkout. Explain that Linux restore needs the pure-Go helper alongside swarm; standalone `go build -o swarm ./cmd/swarm`, `go install ./cmd/swarm`, and versioned `go install .../cmd/swarm@...` supply the CLI only. Preserve these supported CLI-only paths, including compatible-release guidance, with that scope clearly stated. Show real BIN_DIR/GOBIN override examples and installing both extracted release executables together; retain Go-only CLI instructions with their precise scope and existing metadata explanation. Preserve README visuals. State that the helper must be installed next to `swarm` for Linux restore; do not claim current swarm automatically discovers or uses it (runtime integration belongs to #318). Add `changes/unreleased/329.md` with a single `- ` bullet describing only local/release Linux helper packaging. No runtime setup claims beyond the WorkUnit.
5. Run focused and required checks; collect archive operator evidence separately when GoReleaser is unavailable. Review the diff for unchanged runtime files, limits, CLI metadata and non-Linux packaging. No staging, credentials, publishing or gate approval from this agent subprocess.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against the approved contract and source, not authority over gates or validation.

- Entry points: `Makefile:8-23` variables/build/install; `.goreleaser.yaml:5-37` builds/archives; `README.md:75-92` and `docs/project.md:9` installation; proposed `changes/unreleased/329.md` per `docs/developer.md:620-627`. Proposed test entry points: TestMakePackaging, TestReleasePackaging, TestReleasePackagingRejectsInvalidConfig in `internal/packaging/packaging_test.go` after approved-base absence check.
- Existing coverage to preserve: `internal/cli/version_test.go:8,68`; helper runtime tests at `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go:25,104` unchanged. No existing packaging fixture was found; use in-memory config mutations and temporary output directories.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/packaging -run 'Test(MakePackaging|ReleasePackaging)' -count=1`; `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestResolveBuildVersion' -count=1`. Full checks and operator archive checklist are in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Checked assumptions: helper main exists; YAML dependency exists; Make currently omits helper; README and docs/project advertise CLI-only installation; changelog convention and explicit-helper caller boundary were checked; no GoReleaser executable is available. Evidence came from source reads and command lookup. Approved-base absence remains explicitly unverified.
- Reopen if packaging needs runtime discovery/enforcement changes, unsupported GoReleaser options require release workflow changes, or implementation needs credential/service access. Propose follow-up work instead of absorbing #318.
- **What this change breaks:** repository search (using grep because rg is unavailable) for `make build`, `make install`, `goreleaser`, `swarm-restore-helper`, `go build -o swarm`, and `cmd/swarm@` found README.md:78,81 and docs/project.md:9 (update together, retaining CLI-only commands), docs/developer.md:620-627 (preserve convention; add 329 fragment), internal/harness/templates/github/workflows/swarm-fork-coordinator.yml:89 and swarm-validate.yml:34 (preserve supported CLI-only installs unchanged; no runtime integration), .github/workflows/swarm-validate.yml:75 (preserve CLI-only Windows build unchanged), Makefile target descriptions (update), .github/workflows/release.yml:56,80 (preserve unchanged), internal/harness/doctor_drift_test.go:176 GoReleaser action fixture (preserve unchanged), and internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go:25,104 helper builds (preserve unchanged). Existing CLI release ldflags, archive names/formats/docs, README metadata explanation, CLI version tests, and harness command templates remain unchanged. Review consumers against the final diff.

## Operator guidance

> Address only concrete REVIEW.md changes: include docs/project.md installation paragraph alongside README, add scoped changelog329, widen install-command consumer search, use supported v2 ids key, test packaging mutations. Preserve existing supported CLI-only paths and explain Linux helper requirement without claiming automatic discovery/use not implemented. Keep Make/release packaging scope and runtime318 separation. Operator will run real GoReleaser2.18.3 archive verification if sandbox lacks it; do not make unavailable tooling block implementation.

# ISSUE-329 test plan

Planning artifacts only have been produced; the following checks are for implementation. Tests must not execute restore, alter runtime limits, require Bubblewrap, download tools, request credentials, or require artifact services.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Automated coverage and commands | Additional evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC1: Linux make build/install produce both same-checkout binaries; helper forces cgo off; CLI metadata and custom paths survive | `go test ./internal/packaging -run TestMakePackaging -count=1`. On native Linux run real Make build/install into separate temporary BIN_DIR/GOBIN paths containing spaces. Require both executables, correct names/modes, helper main package, GOOS/GOARCH and CGO_ENABLED=0 via debug/buildinfo. Compare CLI metadata to an unstamped same-checkout control and run CLI version. Recording GO wrapper checks ambient CGO_ENABLED=1 cannot enable helper cgo, GO override is honored, effective target OS controls helper selection, custom install/build paths and helper errors propagate. Preserve default path resolution in wrapper assertions. | `go test ./internal/cli -run TestResolveBuildVersion -count=1`; CLI flags must remain unstamped locally. No helper runtime execution. |
| AC2: Linux amd64/arm64 release archives contain matching helper; Darwin/Windows CLI behavior retained | `go test ./internal/packaging -run TestReleasePackaging -count=1`. Parse actual release YAML, verify main packages, helper cgo override, exact matrices, selected archive build IDs under supported v2 `ids` (reject deprecated archive `builds`) and unequal-count handling, CLI ldflags, names/formats/docs. Cross-build helper for both Linux architectures with config-derived settings into temporary outputs; inspect metadata/architecture without executing foreign binaries. Check non-Linux helper exclusion via config and recording Make tests. | Actual archive membership/modes remain covered by the operator checklist below; config tests alone cannot establish GoReleaser grouping correctness. |
| AC3: regressions catch omissions/cgo and executable install paths; docs explain real commands and requirement | The two tests above plus `TestReleasePackagingRejectsInvalidConfig`: in-memory mutations remove helper, omit its archive ID, remove/change CGO_ENABLED=0 or introduce non-Linux/wrong-arch helper targets, and must fail validation. Automated temporary-Makefile mutations remove the helper recipe or remove/change its CGO_ENABLED=0 override for build and install. Run with ambient CGO_ENABLED=1 through the recording wrapper; require the shared packaging assertion to accept the original and reject each mutation for the missing invocation/cgo setting, not an incidental syntax failure. Make wrapper asserts helper invocation exists and forces CGO_ENABLED=0; real metadata checks catch a missing override even where binaries would otherwise appear static. Review README.md and docs/project.md installation commands against Makefile and Go package paths; preserve and label direct go build/go install paths as CLI-only. Validate the single packaging-scoped bullet in changes/unreleased/329.md with `go run ./cmd/changelog --check` and `make check`. | Check edited relative links/anchors and parse edited bash snippets from both README.md and docs/project.md with `bash -n` (substitute a concrete compatible version for prose placeholders); ensure Linux release instructions install both files beside each other and direct Go CLI installation is accurately scoped. Both docs must explain the Linux helper belongs next to swarm, without claiming automatic discovery/use or runtime integration from #318. |

Real Make tests may skip only on explicitly unsupported host OS, with a reason; native Linux CI/operator execution must cover them. Do not skip missing-helper/cgo assertions or report a skipped artifact check as passed. Use scratch/temp outputs, not a user's real install directory. Metadata assertions should require CGO_ENABLED=0, not infer purity merely from successful compilation or executable mode.

## Focused checks

```bash
go test ./internal/packaging -run 'Test(MakePackaging|ReleasePackaging)' -count=1
go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestResolveBuildVersion' -count=1
```

Independently review mutation tests: demonstrate that removing the helper recipe/config selection or its cgo override makes the relevant test fail. Keep mutations in temporary fixtures, never production runtime code. Inspect the implementation diff for unintended runtime or workflow edits.

## Required validation after implementation

Run approved commands directly, using writable Go caches as needed:

```bash
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
go run ./cmd/changelog --check
```

`make check` supplies repository race and changelog checks. Do not run `make install` into the host default directory for verification; automated tests use temporary GOBIN. Record any unavailable dependency/environment check with its exact failure and retained coverage obligation.

## Operator checklist: actual release archives

GoReleaser is absent in this agent sandbox. On an operator checkout with the existing pinned v2.18.3 tool and dependencies, without publishing:

```bash
goreleaser check
goreleaser release --snapshot --clean
```

- Inspect all six OS/architecture archives with `tar -tzf`, `tar -tvzf` or `unzip -l` as appropriate. Linux amd64 and arm64 each contain exactly one `swarm` and one `swarm-restore-helper` beside one another; Darwin and Windows each contain only the supported CLI executable, with Windows zip/`.exe` behavior preserved. Verify existing archive naming, README/LICENSE/docs inclusion and checksum manifest coverage.
- Extract Linux archives separately. Use `go version -m` on both helpers to verify CGO_ENABLED=0 and matching GOOS/GOARCH/main package; confirm executable mode on both binaries. Inspect CLI embedded version/commit/date against the snapshot metadata and ensure both products come from the same release checkout. No helper execution is required.
- On matching Linux hosts, install the extracted pair into a temporary directory using the documented commands; require executable files side by side and run only `swarm version`. Foreign architectures need metadata/mode inspection, not emulation or runtime testing.
- Record tool version, commands, archive inventory, metadata and results in PR evidence. If tooling is still unavailable, mark actual archive validation pending explicitly for the operator; implementation need not wait for external artifact services. Do not claim archive validation from YAML tests alone.

Runtime acceptance and bounded diagnostics stay with #318. Live fork flows, non-Linux helper execution and resource-limit verification are outside this WorkUnit.

Preserve existing supported CLI-only paths and explain Linux helper requirement without claiming automatic discovery/use not implemented. Keep Make/release packaging scope and runtime318 separation. Operator will run real GoReleaser2.18.3 archive verification if sandbox lacks it; do not make unavailable tooling block implementation.

Temporary Makefile mutations (helper recipe removed; CGO_ENABLED=0 removed or changed), run separately for build and install under ambient CGO_ENABLED=1. In-memory config mutations cover a missing build or archive ID, a missing cgo override, and wrong OS/arch. |

## Acceptance coverage

| AC | Coverage | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC1 make build/install pair, forced CGO_ENABLED=0, CLI metadata and caller paths preserved | Real Linux Make runs into temp BIN_DIR/GOBIN with spaces; buildinfo checks; unstamped CLI control; `TestResolveBuildVersion` | Covered |
| AC2 Linux amd64/arm64 archives include helper; Darwin/Windows unchanged | Typed config contract test plus a config-derived Linux cross-build buildinfo check; real archive contents left to the operator checklist (stated honestly) | Covered within sandbox limits |
| AC3 regressions catch an omitted helper or cgo build; docs accurate | Mutation suites above; docs checks; no auto-discovery claim | Covered |

## Scope and constraints

- No changes to runtime, resource limits, protocol, adapters, discovery, workflows, or dependencies. Runtime acceptance stays with #318. Real archive tooling is an operator checklist and does not block implementation. Live fork, non-Linux execution and helper restore runs are excluded.
- No protected paths are touched. The `allow_harness_changes: true` permission is not needed.

## Advisory (non-blocking)

- Word the docs carefully: say the helper "is installed next to `swarm` for Linux restore" without suggesting that the current `swarm` locates it automatically. The plan already requires this.
- If v2.18.3 rejects `allow_different_binary_count`, reopen as the plan states. Do not edit the release workflow.

# ISSUE-329 implementation

Implemented the independently approved corrected packaging plan in order.

1. Make build/install resolve the effective target OS using the selected GO executable and include the existing helper only for Linux. Helper invocations explicitly set CGO_ENABLED=0. CLI flags and local version stamping remain unchanged. Output paths, GOBIN and GO executable paths are quoted; installation still invokes the installed CLI version command.
2. GoReleaser selects the existing CLI build and a Linux amd64/arm64 helper build through archive ids with allow_different_binary_count. Existing CLI flags, platform matrix, archive names, formats, documentation files and checksums remain unchanged.
3. Added test-only packaging coverage: typed real release configuration validation, config mutations, actual Linux Make outputs and same-checkout CLI metadata control comparison, config-derived helper cross-builds and buildinfo inspection, recording-wrapper checks for Linux/Darwin/Windows and default/custom paths, helper failure propagation, and independent build/install recipe omission and cgo mutations. Original fixtures pass before mutated fixtures are rejected. Helpers are never executed.
4. Updated README and docs/project together with Linux release pair installation, same-checkout Make installation, paths with spaces, and explicitly scoped CLI-only Go commands. Added the single-bullet 329 fragment. No automatic helper discovery/use claim was added.
5. Ran focused and required checks as recorded below.

Only the packaging/configuration/documentation/test files listed below were changed. Runtime code, runtime tests (including #318), resource limits, release workflow versions and dependencies were untouched. No coordinator staging, credential access or publishing was attempted.

## Evidence and limitations

- This snapshot has no Git metadata. git ls-tree HEAD internal/packaging changes/unreleased/329.md failed with “not a git repository”. Both paths were absent locally before creation; their absence at the approved base remains for the coordinator to confirm. No existing files at these paths were overwritten.
- command -v goreleaser found no executable. Actual GoReleaser v2.18.3 check/snapshot/archive inventory/mode/checksum and release metadata validation remain pending with the operator's pinned temporary tool. YAML and cross-build tests do not establish actual archive generation.
- All documentation bash snippets parse and relative file links exist in both edited guides; edited installation prose introduces no new local anchors.
- Tests use temporary output directories and never install into the host default directory.
- Shell startup emitted “Failed to create stream fd: Operation not permitted”; commands listed as passed still returned zero.
